Reciprocal

/rih-SIP-ruh-kul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Reciprocal means given, felt, or done in return — shared equally in both directions by both sides.

The two nations signed a reciprocal trade agreement, each cutting taxes on the other's goods.

Worked Example

The climbing partners built a reciprocal trust over the years: each one checks the other's harness before every single ascent.

The trust runs in both directions — each climber gives the same care and receives it back. That two-way flow is exactly what makes it reciprocal.

How Reciprocal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

mutual

mutual: shared equally by both sides

two-way

two-way: flowing in both directions

returned

returned: given back in kind

Antonyms

one-way

one-way: moving in a single direction only

lopsided

lopsided: unbalanced, favoring one side

How Strong Is It? — shared → reciprocal → interdependent

shared vs. reciprocal

shared vs. reciprocal: A shared interest just means two people like the same thing; a reciprocal bond means each one actively gives something back to the other.

interdependent vs. reciprocal

interdependent vs. reciprocal: A reciprocal partnership trades favors back and forth, but an interdependent one goes further — neither side could function alone.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back, backward (Latin)

Root — -cipro-

Root — -cipro-: forward (from Latin pro; Latin reciprocus meant 'moving backward and forward, alternating')

Suffix — -cal

Suffix — -cal: adjective ending (a variant of -al, 'relating to')

Put it together

Put it together: Reciprocal literally means 'going back and forward' — like a favor that travels from you to a friend and then comes back again.

Use the root in a new word: reciprocity

Use the root in a new word: reciprocity: The two towns practice reciprocity: firefighters from each one answer emergency calls across the border whenever they're needed.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal — academic and everyday

Reciprocal describes an arrangement, feeling, or action that flows equally in both directions: reciprocal trust, a reciprocal favor, a reciprocal agreement. Cross-reference: the related verb form, reciprocate ('to give something in return'), names the action itself — reciprocal is the adjective that describes the two-way relationship itself. If only one side gives, the relationship is one-way, not reciprocal.
